content: 1. Phenobarbital is metabolized by the hepatic enzyme CYP3A4. Exercise caution and monitor when using this drug. Avoid concurrent use of strong CYP3A inducers. 2. Belladonna alkaloids and cyclizine both reduce cholinergic effects and transmission. Cyclizine and phenobarbital both enhance sedation. Use caution and monitor. 3. Phenobarbital and cyclobenzaprine both increase sedation. Belladonna alkaloids and cyclobenzaprine both reduce cholinergic effects and transmission. Use caution and monitor. 4. Phenobarbital reduces the level or effect of cyclophosphamide by altering hepatic enzyme CYP2B6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 5. Belladonna alkaloids and darifenacin both reduce cholinergic effects and transmission. Use caution and monitor. 6. Phenobarbital reduces the level or effect of cyclosporine by altering hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism and by affecting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 7. Cyproheptadine and phenobarbital both enhance sedation. Use caution and monitor. 8. Phenobarbital and dantrolene both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor. 9. Phenobarbital reduces the level or effect of daprodustat through other mechanisms. Modify therapy and monitor closely. CYP2C8 inducers may decrease daprodustat exposure, potentially reducing efficacy. Monitor hemoglobin and adjust daprodustat dose when initiating or discontinuing CYP2C8 inducers. 10. Phenobarbital increases the toxicity of topical dapsone by altering its metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. This interaction may induce methemoglobinemia. 11. Phenobarbital and daridorexant both increase sedation. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Co-administration increases the risk of CNS depression, potentially impairing psychomotor performance and causing daytime impairment. 12. Phenobarbital reduces the level or effect of darifenacin by altering hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 13. Phenobarbital reduces the level or effect of dasatinib by altering hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 14. Phenobarbital decreases levels of deferasirox through other mechanisms. Use caution and monitor. Avoid concurrent use of potent UGT inducers with deferasirox. If co-administration is necessary, consider increasing the initial dose of deferasirox to 30 mg/kg and monitor ferritin levels and clinical response. 15. Phenobarbital reduces the level or effect of deflazacort by affecting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 16. Phenobarbital and desipramine both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor. 17. Desloratadine and phenobarbital both enhance sedation. Use caution and monitor. 18. Phenobarbital reduces the level or effect of dexamethasone by altering hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism and by affecting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 19. Dexbrompheniramine and phenobarbital both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor. 20. Dexchlorpheniramine and phenobarbital both enhance sedation. Use caution and monitor. 21. Phenobarbital increases sedation, while dexfenfluramine decreases it. The effect of this interaction is unclear; use caution and monitor. 22. Phenobarbital and dexmedetomidine both enhance sedation. Use caution and monitor. 23. Phenobarbital increases sedation, while dexmethylphenidate decreases it. The effect of this interaction is unclear; use caution and monitor. 24. Phenobarbital increases sedation, while dextroamphetamine decreases it. The effect of this interaction is unclear; use caution and monitor. 25. Phenobarbital and dextromoramide both enhance sedation. Use caution and monitor. 26. Phenobarbital and diamorphine both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor. 27. Phenobarbital reduces the level or effect of diazepam by altering hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Phenobarbital and diazepam both enhance sedation. Use caution and monitor. 28. Diazepam buccal and phenobarbital both increase sedation. Either drug enhances the effects of the other through pharmacodynamic synergism. Use caution and monitor. Phenobarbital reduces the level or effect of diazepam buccal by altering hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 29. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inducers may increase the elimination rate of diazepam, potentially reducing its efficacy. Use caution and monitor. 30. Phenobarbital reduces the level or effect of diazepam intranasal by altering hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Diazepam intranasal and phenobarbital both enhance sedation. Either drug increases the effects of the other through pharmacodynamic synergism. Use caution and monitor. 31. Belladonna alkaloids and dicyclomine both reduce cholinergic effects and transmission. Use caution and monitor. 32. Phenobarbital increases sedation, while diethylpropion decreases it. The effect of this interaction is unclear; use caution and monitor. 33. Difelikefalin and phenobarbital both enhance sedation. Use caution and monitor. 34. Phenobarbital and diphenoxylate HCl both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor. 35. Belladonna alkaloids decrease cholinergic effects, while donepezil increases them. The effect of this interaction is unclear; use caution and monitor. 36. Phenobarbital and dipipanone both enhance sedation. Use caution and monitor. 37. Phenobarbital increases sedation, while dobutamine decreases it. The effect of this interaction is unclear; use caution and monitor. 38. Phenobarbital reduces the level or effect of docetaxel by affecting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 39. Phenobarbital increases sedation, while dopamine decreases it. The effect of this interaction is unclear; use caution and monitor. 40. Phenobarbital increases sedation, while dopexamine decreases it. The effect of this interaction is unclear; use caution and monitor. 41. Belladonna alkaloids and dosulepin both reduce cholinergic effects and transmission. Phenobarbital and dosulepin both enhance sedation. Use caution and monitor. 42. Phenobarbital and doxepin both increase sedation. Belladonna alkaloids and doxepin both reduce cholinergic effects and transmission. Use caution and monitor. 43. Phenobarbital reduces the level or effect of doxorubicin by altering hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism and by increasing elimination. Use caution and monitor. 44. Belladonna alkaloids reduce the levels of droperidol by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Belladonna alkaloids also reduce droperidol levels through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Droperidol enhances the effects of belladonna alkaloids through pharmacodynamic synergism. Use caution and monitor. Additive anticholinergic effects and possible hypoglycemia may occur. 45. Phenobarbital reduces the level or effect of doxorubicin liposomal by altering hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism and by increasing elimination. Use caution and monitor. 46. Phenobarbital decreases doxycycline levels by increasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 47. Phenobarbital and doxylamine both enhance sedation. Use caution and monitor. 48. Phenobarbital reduces the level or effect of dronabinol by altering hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Dronabinol is a CYP3A4 substrate. 49. Phenobarbital and droperidol both enhance sedation. Use caution and monitor. 50. Dulaglutide slows gastric emptying and may affect the absorption of concurrently administered oral medications. Be particularly cautious when co-administering drugs with a narrow therapeutic index. Use caution and monitor. 51. Dupilumab may normalize the formation of CYP450 enzymes by reducing cytokine levels during chronic inflammation. When initiating or discontinuing dupilumab in patients receiving concomitant CYP450 substrates, particularly those with a narrow therapeutic index, monitor for therapeutic effects. Use caution and monitor. 52. Phenobarbital reduces the level or effect of duvelisib by affecting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 53. Echothiophate iodide increases cholinergic effects, while belladonna alkaloids decrease them. The effect of this interaction is unclear; use caution and monitor. 54. Elagolix increases the level or effect of phenobarbital by altering hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Elagolix is a weak CYP2C19 inhibitor. Phenobarbital reduces the level or effect of elagolix by altering hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 55. Phenobarbital reduces the level or effect of eletriptan by altering hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 56. Elranatamab increases the level or effect of phenobarbital by altering hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Elranatamab causes cytokine release syndrome (CRS), which may suppress CYP enzyme activity, leading to increased exposure to CYP substrates. This is more likely to occur during the initiation of elranatamab step-up dosing and up to 14 days after the first treatment dose, as well as during and after CRS. Use caution and monitor. 57. Phenobarbital reduces the level or effect of eltrombopag by altering hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 and CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 58. Enasidenib reduces the level or effect of phenobarbital by altering hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Enasidenib, a weak CYP3A4 inducer, may decrease systemic exposure to CYP3A4 substrates. Monitor and adjust the dose of the substrate as clinically indicated. Use caution and monitor. 59. Phenobarbital reduces the level or effect of enfortumab vedotin by altering hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 60. Epcoritamab causes cytokine release, which may suppress CYP enzyme activity, leading to increased exposure to CYP substrates. For certain CYP substrates, minimal changes in their concentration may lead to serious adverse reactions. If needed, modify therapy as recommended in the substrate's prescribing information. Use caution and monitor. 61. Phenobarbital increases sedation, while ephedrine decreases it. The effect of this interaction is unclear; use caution and monitor. 62. Phenobarbital increases sedation, while epinephrine decreases it. The effect of this interaction is unclear; use caution and monitor. 63. Phenobarbital increases sedation, while racemic epinephrine decreases it. The effect of this interaction is unclear; use caution and monitor. 64. Phenobarbital reduces the level or effect of erlotinib by altering hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 65. Phenobarbital reduces the level or effect of escitalopram by altering hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 66. Phenobarbital reduces the level or effect of eslicarbazepine acetate by increasing its metabolism. Higher dosages of eslicarbazepine may be necessary. Eslicarbazepine acetate increases the level or effect of phenobarbital by altering hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 67. Phenobarbital decreases esmolol levels by increasing its metabolism. Consider a higher beta-blocker dose during co-administration of phenobarbital. Atenolol, sotalol, and nadolol are less likely to be affected than other beta-blockers. Use caution and monitor. 68. Phenobarbital reduces the level or effect of esomeprazole by altering hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 69. Phenobarbital and estazolam both enhance sedation. Use caution and monitor. 70. Phenobarbital reduces the level or effect of estradiol by altering hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism and by affecting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 71. Phenobarbital reduces the level or effect of estradiol vaginal by altering hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 72. Phenobarbital reduces the level or effect of conjugated synthetic estrogens by altering hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism and by affecting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 73. Phenobarbital reduces the level or effect of esterified estrogens by altering hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 74. Phenobarbital reduces the level or effect of estropipate by altering hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism and by affecting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 75. Eszopiclone and phenobarbital both enhance sedation. Use caution and monitor. 76. Phenobarbital and ethanol both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor. 77. Phenobarbital reduces the level or effect of ethosuximide by altering hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 78. Phenobarbital reduces the level or effect of ethotoin by altering hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 79. Etomidate and phenobarbital both enhance sedation. Use caution and monitor. 80. Phenobarbital reduces the level or effect of etonogestrel by altering hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 81. Phenobarbital reduces the level or effect of etoposide by altering hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 82. Phenobarbital reduces the level or effect of etravirine by altering hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 and CYP2C9 metabolism. Use caution and monitor.
